newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-HOLDER FALLS NINE SHORT OF MAIDEN TEST CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HOLDER FALLS NINE SHORT OF MAIDEN TEST CENTURY.

text.p: Barbadian Roland Holder fell nine short of a maiden test century on Saturday as the West Indies were dismissed for 296 in their first innings on the second day of the second test.
West Indies, 239 for seven overnight, lost their last three wickets for seven runs, starting with Holder's departure on 91.
Holder, who resumed on 71, played over a delivery from left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi and was bowled leg-stump. His 239-ball innings had lasted 293 minute and contained seven fours.
Captain Courtney Walsh was next out, caught behind off Sauray Ganguly without scoring after facing just three balls.
Fast bowler Franklyn Rose struck 34, including two sixes and two fours and shared in a stand of 69 with Holder, a West Indies' eighth-wicket record against India.
Leg-spinner Anil Kumble captured five for 104 off 38 overs, with Joshi taking three for 79.
